subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equations of the two straight lines through (1,3) which are (1) parallel to and (2) perpendicular to the line joining the points (3,−5) and (−6,1).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 38, book p.147. The stem is kept as ONE object: a single setup with two riders under one instruction, as printed; the printed enumerators (1) and (2) are set inline and read awkwardly, and are reproduced here as parts. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split is one mark per rider, because each rider is a complete answer on its own; the shared slope of the join is done inside part (1), where it is first needed. Perpendicularity was confirmed numerically, not assumed: m₁m₂ = (−2/3)(3/2) = −1, and the normals (2, 3) and (3, −2) have dot product 6 − 6 = 0. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you compute once and use twice, and how the two required slopes come from it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Part (1) the parallel line
steps.margin_note: First mark. The slope of the join is computed once and used by both parts. A parallel line keeps that slope exactly.
steps.memory_tip: Parallel keeps the slope unchanged. Find the slope of the join once and reuse it for both parts.
lines: Slope of AB  m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)
(1) The parallel line has the same slope

recall.must_convey: That the slope of AB is −2/3 and the parallel line through (1, 3) is 2x + 3y − 11 = 0.
accept: slope of the join is six over minus nine which is minus two by three
y minus three equals minus two by three into x minus one
the parallel line is two x plus three y minus eleven equals zero
heard_as: two x plus three y minus eleven

steps.why: Both riders depend on the same number, the slope of AB, so it is worth computing carefully once; parallel lines are exactly the lines with that same slope.
common_mistakes: Computing the slope as (x₂ − x₁)/(y₂ − y₁), upside down.
Sign slip in 1 − (−5), giving −4 instead of 6.

steps.label: Part (2) the perpendicular line
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Flip the slope and change its sign, then check m₁m₂ = −1 before writing the line — that check is what catches a swap with no sign change.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular: flip the slope and change the sign. Then check m₁m₂ = −1 before you write the line.

recall.must_convey: That the perpendicular slope is 3/2 and the line through (1, 3) is 3x − 2y + 3 = 0.
accept: perpendicular slope is minus one over m which is three by two
flip the slope and change the sign
check that the product of the slopes is minus one
perpendicular kabatti minus one by m
the perpendicular line is three x minus two y plus three equals zero
heard_as: three x minus two y plus three

steps.why: Swapping the coefficients of a line without changing exactly one sign gives a line that still passes through the point but is not perpendicular, and the answer then looks right. Computing m₁m₂ and seeing −1 is what rules that out.
common_mistakes: Writing 3x + 2y + k = 0, which swaps the coefficients but changes no sign.
Using the same slope −2/3 for both parts.
